questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I would say that it has been a mix between academic opportunities as well as my wish to explore new cultures in the middle east, where it will also be easier for me to further advance my communicative skills in arabic, as well as seeing and experiencing the daily life, norms and traditions from up close instead of through books and movies.
This exchange has also allowed me to meet a lot of different people from all-around the globe and exchange our thoughts on several topics and future ideas and hopes.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
In the beginning it was hard to get into the daily life and get accustomed to living in a different place and culture, but I think both the staff at the university as well as my companions from DK helped me easing myself into the life and experience of it all
Overall I have enjoyed my stay, some of the classes could have been better structured level-vise (the egyptian dialect), but I also think a bit more preparation from my side would have helped it.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think it was easy to get around and everyone was helpful whenever I had any problems, I could be from the staff at different hostels, the airport, the university or the people on the streets, I found it easy to find information and help

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
We were offered assistance with arrival from the airport and accommodation by the university and we had a lecture on the different subjects and things we needed to be prepared for on the first day of our university.
In this class we were told about general norms and what to be careful of by the teacher and got several recommendations for restaurants and cultural experiences we could enjoy during our stay.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
We had some trouble with it, but there was a lot of different possibilities for housing, we were just unlucky, and the institution did offer it's help in finding housing off campus as well
It worked for us to find some local brokers who could help us with the apartments and everything and both the teachers and university were willing to help with suggestions and help if needed, but be prepared to spend some time looking and have a hostel prepared for the first week so that you can check that everything works at your accommodation

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
In Egypt there are a lot of different neighborhoods with varying degrees of local life and vibes, I enjoyed both down town and Ibrahamiyya, but do think of the location and distance from your university as some can be quite far
There are plenty of opportunities to be part of the local life and get friends as long as you are ready to try a few different things as well as open-minded

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
It really does depend on what you find, I think the other students enjoyed their accommodations but we had to move between 3 apartments
the first time was because the kitchen and bathroom had some problems our landlord promised to fix, but never did
the second because of termites, which couldn't have been avoided
but our second and third apartments were great.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was quite easy and we were guided through the registration back in Denmark and didn't have to change anything after our arrival

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Guided classes and the chancellors' help

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: We had an obligatory stay and had to take 3 predetermined classes

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I have no advice other than asking for help with the chancellors if you are worried or unsure of anything

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I quite enjoyed all the classes and the program itself, the dialect class was quite quick and it's books not always too focused on the process but only the language
But otherwise I did enjoy all the classes and the teachers were fantastic

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
I think the level was quite good, we had different classes at the literature and MSA classes but dialect was all of us together
I think we were supposed to get to intermediate high after our course but I ended up somewhere in-between mid and high

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
In my opinion it was quite different, at TAFL we focused on furthering our knowledge and how we could read without a dictionary or glossary, but then again back at UCPH we had to start learning a new language
But overall TAFL had a more pedagogical approach on how you acquire a language

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Modern Standard Arabic (MSA)
Egyptian Colloquial Arabic (ECA)
Arabic Literature 1 - I am returning this summer for a Literature 2 course

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I really enjoyed MSA and literature 1 but it was also great to have the dialect classes so that I could speak other languages than just MSA and thereby also becoming closer to the locals as you spoke their language as well
So I can highly recommend all the courses I had

Housing DKK per month *

Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None that I can remember

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
meat was more expensive than expected and vegetables were much cheaper
I remember normal stuff like brooms and such costing quite a lot but it was quite confusing how some items were cheap and others more expensive than expected, but I cannot remember any specific items or prices at the moment

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I quite liked the extracurriculars but some of them had more of a class feeling than like a club feeling, for example the cooking club which became kind of like a class about what different meats and greens were called and the different techniques names than how to cook different dishes

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: We had calligraphy, cooking, cinema and singing clubs, but I know the Norwegians had some different clubs as well such as journalism

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I enjoyed the calligraphy and cinema clubs

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I can recommend going on small trips to the surrounding cities such as siwa, aswan, luxor, cairo and all those

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I got into the local culture after around 3-4 weeks I think and after I found some local friends that I could hang out with

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: At the moment I can't think of any

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed the open-mindedness of the people and how we could talk with anyone about anything and how easy it was to find partners for a discussion

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Remember that this is also a cultural opportunity and not just a time to study
Focus on developing your language
Enjoy your time and don't stress about the school so that you cannot go out to enjoy the culture and history

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Enjoy your time and keep in contact with both the locals and other exchange students

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
I would say it is both the advancement of my Arabic and my new cultural view on several topics and experiences
I don't just know about the different traditions and norms but have experienced them and the impact that religion has on a whole society and how people can coexist

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Sometimes I could get homesick and feel alone in a different part of the world, but you can always remember that the others are probably experiencing the same, and that this is a new and exciting experience

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
